description:
Donations are tax deductible and we need your support to continue our work. Text-to-donate, text VSRF to 53555.Show more This week on VSRF Live, we confront one of the most urgent issues of our time: mental health, suicide, and the institutions shaping how we’re allowed to talk about both.
Joining us:
Kim Witczak – international drug safety advocate and founder of WoodyMatters, whose husband Woody died by suicide shortly after being prescribed an antidepressant. Since then, Kim has served on FDA advisory committees and become a leading voice demanding transparency about psychiatric drug risks.
Dr. Roger McFillin, Psy.D. – clinical psychologist and host of the top-ranked Radically Genuine Podcast. Known for his unfiltered critique of modern psychiatry, he challenges over-medicalization, diagnostic labeling, and the assumption that healing requires lifelong medication.
Danielle Gansky – psychiatric drug harm advocate whose platforms reach more than 450,000 people. Placed on psychiatric medications at just seven years old, Danielle entered years of polypharmacy. Two doctor-directed tapers — along with an adverse reaction to an antipsychotic — left her severely injured. She is still healing today while working to safely taper and advocating for reforms to prevent similar harm to others.
Together, we examine:
Antidepressants and suicide risk
The impact of medicating children
Withdrawal, tapering, and informed consent
Regulatory oversight of psychiatric drugs
The commodification of mental health
What real resilience and recovery demand
Is the current system helping those in despair — or creating new harm in the name of treatment?
This conversation is not about stigma. It’s about evidence. It’s about informed consent. It’s about the courage to ask hard questions.
Join us for a candid discussion about grief, accountability, and what it truly means to protect mental health in challenging times. Show less
